newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat leaves for talks with Egypt's Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Arafat leaves for talks with Egypt's Mubarak.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Monday left Gaza for Egypt where he will try to persuade President Hosni Mubarak to join a Washington summit to end violence between Israel and the Palestinians, witnesses said.

Israel agreed to President Bill Clinton's call on Sunday for a summit with Arab leaders in Washington on the violence -- sparked by Israel's policies in Jerusalem -- in which 55 Palestinians and 14 Israelis have been killed.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he has no plans to close a controversial Jerusalem tunnel that touched off clashes between protesters and Israeli troops and gunbattles between Israeli and Palestinian forces last week.

Israel's opening of the tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, whose final status is a matter of hot dispute between Israelis and Arabs, combined with festering Palestinian frustration over Netanyahu's policies and ignited the gun battles.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told CBS television that Mubarak wanted some assurance that Israel would honour its past agreements with the Palestinians before agreeing to attend the summit that is to include Jordan's King Hussein.

Clinton telephoned Arafat on Sunday to invite him to a Washington summit but the Palestinian president withheld his agreement to attend, a PLO official said, pending Mubarak's participation. U.S. officials said they expected Arafat to attend.
